questions.question: The simple interest on a sum of money at 10% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 8,100. What would be the compound interest (in Rs.) on the same sum for the same period at 15% p. a., when the interest is compounded yearly? (nearest to Rs. 1)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

R = 10%

T = 2 years

SI = Rs.8,100

R₂ for CI = 15%

**Formula Used:**

S.I. = (P × R × T)/100

A = P(1+ R/100)T

C.I. = A – P

Where, 

P → Principle

T → Time

R → Rate

A → Amount 

**Calculation:**

S.I. = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ 8,100 = (P × 2 × 10)/100

⇒ 8,100 = P/5

⇒ P = 5 × 8,100

⇒ P = 40,500

Now for C.I.

A = P(1+ R/100)T

⇒ A = 40,500(1 + 15/100)² 

⇒ A = 40,500(1 +3/20)²

⇒ A = 40,500(23/20)² 

⇒ A = 40,500 × (23/20) × (23/20)

⇒ A = 53561.25

CI = A – P

⇒ C.I. = 53561.25 – 40500 = Rs. 13,061.25 ≈ Rs. 13,061

**∴ The required compound interest is Rs. 13,061**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**10% for 2 years = 20% of principle = 8100

⇒ 20P/100 = 8100

⇒ P = 40500

Equivalent rate of interest for 2 years = 15 + 15 + (15 × 15)/100 = 32.25%

C.I. = 32.25% of 40500

⇒ 32.25 × 40500 /100 = Rs. 13061.25 ≈ Rs. 13061

∴ The required CI is Rs. 13061.

questions.question: The HCF of two numbers is 29, and the other two factors of their LCM are 15 and 13. The smaller of the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
Given:

HCF of two numbers = 29

Other two factors of their LCM = 15 and 13

Concept Used:

The HCF of a group of numbers will be always a factor of their LCM.

HCF is the product of all common prime factors using the least power of each common prime factor.

LCM is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors.

Calculation:

HCF of the two numbers = 29

HCF will be always a factor of LCM.

So, 29 is a factor of the LCM. 

The other two factors in the LCM are 13 and 15.

Factors of the LCM are 29, 13, and 15.

So, Numbers can be taken as (29 × 13) and (29 × 15) = 377 and 435

∴ The smallest number is 377.

questions.question: The average age of 40 students of a class is 16 years. After admission of 10 new students to the class, the average becomes 15 years. If the average age of 5 of the new students is 11 years, then the average age (in years) of the remaining 5 new students is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average age of 40 students = 16 years

On admission of 10 new students average = 15 years

Average of 5 new students = 11

**Formula used:**

{{Average}} = frac{{{{sum of all the values}}}}{{{{number of values}}}}

**Calculation:**

Sum of all ages of 40 students = 40 × 16

⇒ 640 years

After admission of 10 new students, number of students now = 40 + 10

⇒ 50

Sum of all ages after the admission of 10 new students = 50 × 15

⇒ 750 years

Sum of ages of 5 new students = 5 × 11

⇒ 55 years

Now remaining ages of 5 new students = Sum of all ages after the admission of 10 new students - Sum of all ages of 40 students - Sum of ages of 5 new students

⇒ 750 – 640 – 55

⇒ 750 – 695

⇒ 55 years

Average of 5 new students = 55/5

⇒ 11

**Hence, the Average of 5 new students is 11.**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 36,000 is divided into two parts, A and B, such that the simple interest at the rate of 15% p.a. on A and B after two years and four years, respectively, is equal. The total interest (in Rs.) received from A is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 36,000

Rate of interest = 15%

Time for A and B = 2 years and 4 years respectively

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = (principal × rate × time)/100

**Calculation:**

Let Principle for A be Rs. X

Then principal for B = 36,000 - X

Simple interest for A = (X × 15 × 2)/100

⇒ 30X/100

⇒ 0.3X

Simple interest for B = [(36,000 – X) × 15 × 4]/100

⇒ 0.6 × (36,000 – X)

⇒ 21600 – 0.6X

Now, simple interest of A in 2 years = simple interest for B in 4 years.

0.3X = 21600 – 0.6X

⇒ 0.3X + 0.6X = 21600

⇒ 0.9X = 21600

⇒ X = 21600/0.9

⇒ X = 24000

Then simple interest of A in two years = 0.3X

⇒ 0.3 × 24000

⇒ 7200

**∴ The simple interest of A is Rs. 7200.**

questions.question: In an entrance examination at different centres, a total of 25, 30, 40, 45, 60 and 100 students appeared. The pass percentages of the different centres are 20%, 30%, 35%, 40%, 50% and 75%, respectively. The pass percentage of the entrance examination is: (correct to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The Number of students has given at different centers are 25, 30, 40, 45, 60, and 100

and passing percentages has given on respective centres are 20%, 30%, 35%, 40%, 50% and 75%.

**Formula used:**

Pass percentages = (total number of pass students/total number of appeared students) × 100

A number of passing students at individual centers = a number of students on centers × given the percentage of that center.

**Calculation:**

Let the center's names are A, B, C, D, E, and F.

Number of passing students at centres A = 25 × 20%

⇒ 5

Number of passing students at centres B = 30 × 30%

⇒ 9

Number of passing students at centres C = 40 × 35%

⇒ 14

Number of passing students at centres D = 45 × 40%

⇒ 18

Number of passing students at centres E = 60 × 50%

⇒ 30

And Number of passing students at centres F = 100 × 75%

⇒ 75

Now total number of passing students = 5 + 9 + 14 + 18 + 30 + 75

⇒ 151

Total number of students appeared = 25 + 30 + 40 + 45 + 60 + 100

⇒ 300

Pass percentages = (151/300) × 100

⇒ 50.33%

**Hence, the passing percentage, nearest to the integer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

**{{Passing percentages}} = frac{{{{summation of }}( {{{number of students appeared at centres }} times {{ their passing percentages respectively}}} )}}{{{{total number of students appeared at centres}}}} times 100**

Passing percentages = [(25 × 20% + 30 × 30% + 40 × 35% + 45 × 40% + 60 × 50% + 100 × 75%)/(25 + 30 + 40 + 45 + 60 + 100)] × 100

⇒ [(5 + 9 + 14 + 18 + 30 + 75)/300] × 100

⇒ [151/300] × 100

⇒ 50.33%

**Hence, the passing percentage, nearest to the integer is 50%.**

questions.question: If a² + b² = 82 and ab = 9, then a possible value of a³ + b³ is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify two numbers whose **product (ab)** is 9 and **sum of squares (a²+b²)** is 82.

By inspection, let **a = 9** and **b = 1**.

Check: **9² + 1² = 81 + 1 = 82** and **9 × 1 = 9** (Conditions satisfied).

Now, **a³ + b³ = 9³ + 1³ = 729 + 1 = 730**.

**∴ The correct answer is 730.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: **a² + b² = 82** and **ab = 9**

Formula used: **(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab** and **a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² + b² − ab)**

⇒ (a + b)² = 82 + 2 × 9

⇒ (a + b)² = 82 + 18 = 100

⇒ **a + b = √100 = 10**

⇒ a³ + b³ = (10) × (82 − 9)

⇒ a³ + b³ = 10 × 73

⇒ **a³ + b³ = 730**

**∴ The correct answer is 730.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of Cubes Identity

The factorized form is **a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)** or **(a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b)**.

Difference of Cubes Identity

The factorized form is **a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)**.

Square of a Binomial

Standard expansions are **(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²** and **(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²**.</p

questions.question: P and Q together can do a work in 12 days. P alone can do the same work in 36 days. In how many days can Q alone complete two-third part of the same work?

Q complete the work of = 24/2 = 12 days 

Hence Q complete the work in = **12 days**

questions.question: In a school, 5/12 of the number of students are girls and the rest are boys. 4/7 of the number of boys are below 14 years of age, and 2/5 of the number of girls are 14 years or above 14 years of age. If the number of students below 14 years of age is 1120, then the total number of students in the school is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The no. of girls is 5/12 of the total no. of students

The no. of boys below 14 years of age is 4/7 of the total no. of boys.

The no. of girls 14 years or above 14 years of age is 2/5 of the total no. of girls.

Total no. of student below 14 years of age is 1120.

**Calculation:**

Let the total no. of students be x

The total no. of girls = 5x/12 

Then, the no. of boys = x - 5x/12 = 7x/12

The no. of below 14 years of age = 4/7 × 7x/12 = x/3

The no. of girls 14 years or above 14 years of age = 2/5 × 5x/12 = x/6

The no. of girls below 14 years = 5x/12 - x/6 = 3x/12 = x/4

Total no. of students below 14 years = x/3 + x/4 = 7x/12

According to the question

⇒ 7x/12 = 1120

⇒ x = 1920

**The total number of students is 1920**

questions.question: A train covers 400 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 10 km/h more, it would have taken 2 hours less for the same journey. What is the usual time taken (in hours) by it to complete the journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A train covers total distance = 400km

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance covered/Time taken

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the train be x

Time taken by train = 400/x

Now, the increased speed of train be(x + 10)

Now, Time taken by train = 400/(x + 10)

According to the question;

Difference between time taken = 2 hours

⇒ 400/x - 400/(x + 10) = 2

⇒ 1/x - 1/(x + 10) = 2/400

Rightarrow frac{{( {x + 10 - x} )}}{{( {x + 10} )x}} = frac{{1}}{200}

⇒ 10 × 200 = x² + 10x

⇒ x² + 10x = 2000

⇒ x² + 10x - 2000 = 0

⇒ x = - 50, 40

The speed of the train = 40 km/hr

Time taken by train = 400/40 = 10 hours

**∴ The usual time taken by the train to complete the journey is 10 hours**.
